linear lookup rather than a map + order list: 500 entries is the ceiling, lookups happen
once per transition, and one structure cannot drift from itself. Re-posing an existing
key removes it and appends it (refreshed `Detail`, `At`): the newest failure is the last
to be evicted. Posing a new key with 500 held drops index 0.

**Never on disk.** Nothing in `internal/jobs` imports `os`, `io/ioutil`, `internal/cache`
or `internal/config`; step 4 makes that a test.

### Transitions — where the memory is written

| Event (registry method) | Effect on failures |
|---|---|
| `Start(run)` | for each item: delete `(run.Kind, TargetKey(item.Target), run.Context)` — a new attempt is admitted (criteria 1, 2) |
| `Discover(kind, target, …)` adding a target to the open run | delete its key (the clone's targets are admitted here, not in `Start`) |
| an item reaches `ItemFailed` (via `advance` or `Discover`) | pose `(run.Kind, target, run.Context)` with `Detail`, `Display`, `At = now()` — if `run.Kind.Remembered()` |
| an item reaches `ItemDone` | delete its key (criterion 2) |
| an item of `KindDelete` reaches `ItemDone` | additionally `forget(target, run.Context)` — every kind (criterion 3) |
| `Forget(target, context)` (from `ForgetTargetMsg`) | delete every kind for that target in that context |
| `ItemSkipped`, `Cancel`, `CancelItem`, `Seal`, prune of runs | nothing |

One private method holds the rule, `func (r *Registry) record(run *Run, item Item)`,
called from `advance` and `Discover` after the state is written — two call sites, one
rule. The context comes from the run the transition was matched to, so a failure that
lands after a context switch is still filed under the context it ran in.

`forget` also drops keys **under** the target when the target is an absolute path
(`filepath.Rel` does not start with `..`): deleting `~/w/app` deletes `~/w/app/api` too,
and a re-clone at the same place must not resurface the old failure.
Hypothèse (prudent): descendants are cleared for filesystem paths only; forge paths and
image references are matched exactly (an image `nginx/foo` is not a child of `nginx`).

`Forget` is scoped to the **current** context, stamped by the router: the container
engine is per context (`app.container_engine`), so removing an image under podman does not
remove the docker one. Hypothèse (prudent): `ForgetTargetMsg` carries only `Target`, as
the story states; the router supplies the context.

### Target identity — normalize paths, never image references (criterion 8)

```go
// TargetKey is the identity a failure is remembered and looked up under.
func TargetKey(target string) string {
	if filepath.IsAbs(target) {
		return filepath.Clean(target)
	}
	return target
}
```

- **Paths are cleaned**: `/w/app/`, `/w/./app`, `/w/x/../app` → `/w/app`. `ws` and `:sec`
  already pass the same absolute string (the `:sec` row is the workspace cache key, which
  `ws` wrote), so this only guards against a trailing slash or a non-joined path.
- **Image references are kept raw** (`img.Name()`, `repo:tag`). `nginx` and
  `docker.io/library/nginx` stay **two keys**. Reasons, from criterion 8 itself:
  1. the key must be `Item.Target`, i.e. the scan cache key; the cache keys images by
     the raw name and OCI and `:sec` both read it from there, so they already agree.
     A normalized failure key would agree with neither cache.
  2. normalization is wrong on this code base: `Image.Name()` returns `repository`
     **without** a tag for a `<none>` tag, and a reference parser would read that as
     `:latest` — merging an untagged image with `nginx:latest`, a different image.
  3. the engine decides the spelling, and the engine is per context: docker prints
     `nginx`, podman `docker.io/library/nginx`. Within one context — which is all a
     failure is shown in — one engine spells one image one way.
  Images with `Repository == "<none>"` are never scanned or pulled (OCI skips them), so
  they never reach the memory.
- **Where it is applied**: only in the failure key — on write (`record`, `Start`,
  `Discover`, `Forget`) and on read (`FailureFor`, `FailuresOn`). `Item.Target` is **not**
  rewritten: `FindItem` matches transitions emitted by Cmds with the raw target, and
  cleaning one side only would leave a row spinning for the life of the view. This is
  the deliberate reading of "chemins passés par `filepath.Clean` au lancement": the key
  is computed at launch, the item is not changed.

### Broadcast and reading (criterion 6, D5)

`ChangedMsg.Failures []Failure` — a fresh copy per message (`Registry.Failures()`),
every context included, like `Runs`. Readers:

```go
func FailureFor(failures []Failure, kind Kind, target, contextName string) (Failure, bool)
func FailuresOn(failures []Failure, contextName, target string, kinds ...Kind) []Failure // oldest first; no kinds = all
```

A view applies D5 by passing the kinds it can rerun. Cost note: the copy rides every
spinner tick (10 Hz) until A-03 moves the tick to `jobs.FrameMsg`; at the 500 ceiling it
is ~50 KB per message, in practice a handful of entries. Not optimized here.

### Rule 110

The registry is written from `Update` only: `handleStartJobs` (Start), `routeWork` and
the forge-index handlers (Apply), the new `handleForgetTarget` (Forget). No Cmd holds the
registry; views only ever see the copy. `mise run test-race` on `internal/app` and
`internal/jobs` closes each step.

---

## Step 1 — Failure types, `TargetKey`, reader helpers (pure, no registry)

Files: `internal/jobs/failure.go` (new), `internal/jobs/failure_test.go` (new).

Interfaces: `FailureKey`, `Failure`, `MaxFailures`, `TargetKey(string) string`,
`FailureFor(...)`, `FailuresOn(...)` as above.

Tests (table-driven):
- `TestTargetKeyCleansAbsolutePaths`: `/w/app/` → `/w/app`; `/w/./app` → `/w/app`;
  `/w/x/../app` → `/w/app`; `/w/app` unchanged. Windows case (`C:\w\app\` → `C:\w\app`)
  under `runtime.GOOS == "windows"`.
- `TestTargetKeyLeavesReferencesAlone`: `nginx:1.27`, `nginx`, `docker.io/library/nginx`,
  `grp/sub/proj` (forge path), template slug → unchanged.
- `TestTwoSpellingsOfAnImageAreTwoTargets`: `TargetKey("nginx") != TargetKey("docker.io/library/nginx")`;
  `TargetKey("nginx") != TargetKey("nginx:latest")` (the untagged case).
- `TestAFailureIsReadInItsOwnContextOnly`: failure in `a` → `FailureFor(…, "b")` false,
  `"a"` true (criterion 4, pure half).
- `TestFailureForCleansTheTargetItLooksUp`: stored `/w/app`, looked up `/w/app/` → found.
- `TestFailuresOnKeepsOnlyTheKindsAsked`: scan + sync failures on one target;
  `FailuresOn(…, KindScan)` → scan only; no kinds → both, oldest first.

Command: `go test ./internal/jobs -run 'TargetKey|Failure|TwoSpellings'`

Done when: tests pass, `mise run lint` clean. Nothing calls the helpers yet.

## Step 2 — The memory inside `Registry`

Depends on: 1.

Files: `internal/jobs/registry.go`, `internal/jobs/jobs.go` (`Kind.Remembered`),
`internal/jobs/registry_failures_test.go` (new).

Interfaces:
```go
func (k Kind) Remembered() bool                          // Q-A; option A: true for every kind
func (r *Registry) Failures() []Failure                   // copy, oldest first
func (r *Registry) Forget(target, contextName string) bool // true if anything was dropped
// private
func (r *Registry) record(run *Run, item Item)
func (r *Registry) pose(f Failure)
func (r *Registry) clear(key FailureKey) bool
func (r *Registry) forget(target, contextName string) bool
```
`Start` calls `clear` per item after stamping; `advance` and `Discover` call `record`
after writing the state; `Discover` calls `clear` when it appends a new target.

Tests (use the existing `at(moment)` clock helper):
- `TestAFailedItemIsRemembered`: Start scan `ctx` [`/w/app`] → Apply failed, Detail
  "scan failed — check logs" → `Failures()` = one, key `(scan, /w/app, ctx)`, Detail,
  At = clock.
- `TestAFailureOutlivesItsRun`: fail one target, then start and settle 25 other runs
  (`> MaxFinishedRuns`) → the run is pruned, the failure is still there (criterion 1).
- `TestANewAttemptClearsTheFailure`: fail, then `Start` the same kind/target/context →
  cleared **at Start**, before any item runs (criterion 2).
- `TestASuccessClearsTheFailure`: fail; second run's item goes `done` → cleared.
- `TestAnotherKindOrContextIsNotCleared`: fail scan in `a`; Start scan in `b` and sync in
  `a` on the same target → scan/`a` still there.
- `TestASkipDoesNotClear` / `TestCancelDoesNotClear`: a skipped or cancelled retry leaves
  nothing (cleared at Start) and poses nothing.
- `TestOneFailurePerKey`: fail twice on one key → one entry, latest Detail and At.
- `TestADeleteThatSucceedsForgetsTheTarget`: scan and sync failures on `/w/app` and a
  scan failure on `/w/app/api`; delete run `/w/app` → `done` → all three gone; a failure
  on `/w/application` stays (prefix is by path element, not by string).
- `TestForgetIsScopedToOneContext`: failures on `nginx:1.27` in `a` and `b`;
  `Forget("nginx:1.27", "a")` → returns true, `b` stays; second call returns false.
- `TestForgetMatchesReferencesExactly`: `Forget("nginx", ctx)` leaves `nginx/foo:1`.
- `TestTheCloneClearsAtDiscovery`: clone failure on target T in ctx; new open clone run,
  `Discover(clone, T, queued)` → cleared; `Discover(clone, G, failed)` → G posed.
- `TestTheMemoryIsCappedAtFiveHundred`: 501 distinct failures → 500 held, the first gone;
  variant: re-pose key #1 before #501 → #2 is evicted instead.
- `TestFailuresIsACopy`: mutate the returned slice and an element → registry unchanged.
- `TestEveryKindAnswersRemembered`: walks `Kinds()` against the table decided in Q-A
  (option A: all true). This test is the only thing Q-A changes, with `Remembered`'s body.
- `TestANewRegistryRemembersNothing`: `New().Failures()` empty (restart, pure half).

Command: `go test ./internal/jobs && go test -race ./internal/jobs`

Done when: all `internal/jobs` tests pass (existing ones untouched), race clean.

## Step 3 — The router: `ChangedMsg.Failures`, `ForgetTargetMsg`

Depends on: 2. Parallel with 4.

Files: `internal/jobs/message.go`, `internal/app/jobs.go`, `internal/app/app.go`
(one `case`), `internal/app/failures_test.go` (new).

Interfaces:
```go
// internal/jobs/message.go
type ChangedMsg struct { …; Failures []Failure } // copy, every context, oldest first

// ForgetTargetMsg says a target no longer exists, for a removal the registry did not
// run (an image remove). The router stamps the current context.
type ForgetTargetMsg struct{ Target string }
func ForgetTarget(target string) tea.Cmd

// internal/app/jobs.go
func (a *App) changedMsg() jobs.ChangedMsg              // + Failures: a.jobs.Failures()
func (a *App) handleForgetTarget(msg jobs.ForgetTargetMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)
// if a.jobs.Forget(msg.Target, a.currentContext) → a.jobsChanged(); else nil
```
`app.go`: `case jobs.ForgetTargetMsg: return a.handleForgetTarget(msg)` next to
`jobs.CancelItemMsg`.

Tests (`fakeView` + `lastJobs`/`receivedOf`, `testutil.FastTimers(t, &jobSpinnerInterval)`),
driven by **real** view messages through `a.Update` so `routeWork` is exercised:
- `TestAFailureReachesEveryHeldViewAsACopy`: `jobs.StartMsg` (ws scan, `/w/app`) then
  `workspaces.WorkspaceScanCompleteMsg{RepoPath: "/w/app", Error: err}` → the fake view's
  last `ChangedMsg.Failures` holds `(scan, /w/app, default)`; mutating it does not change
  `a.jobs.Failures()` (criterion 6).
- `TestARetryFromAnotherViewClearsTheFailure` (common key, repo): fail from `ws`
  (`WorkspaceScanCompleteMsg`), then `StartMsg` with the `:sec` run for the same path
  (`security` scan run) → cleared. Same with the `ws` target written `/w/app/` → still
  cleared (TargetKey).
- `TestAnImageFailureIsSharedByOCIAndSec` (common key, image): fail via
  `ociresources.ImageScanFinishedMsg{ImageName: "nginx:1.27", Err}`; `StartMsg` of a
  `:sec` scan on `nginx:1.27` clears it; a `:sec` scan on `docker.io/library/nginx:1.27`
  does **not** (documented non-normalization).
- `TestForgetTargetClearsInTheCurrentContextOnly`: failures on `nginx:1.27` in `default`
  and `prod` (runs started with each context via a context switch, or `a.jobs.Start`
  directly with `scanRun("prod", …)`); `Update(jobs.ForgetTargetMsg{"nginx:1.27"})` in
  `default` → `default` gone, `prod` stays, a broadcast went out; a second identical
  message returns a nil Cmd.
- `TestAFailureSurvivesAContextRoundTrip`: fail in `default`; `ContextSwitchCompleteMsg`
  to `prod` → registry still holds it, `FailureFor(…, "prod")` false on the rebuilt
  view's snapshot; back to `default` → true (criterion 4).
- `TestAFailureSurvivesLeavingAndReopeningAView`: fail; `switchView` away and back →
  the re-entered view's `ChangedMsg` (from `sendJobsTo`) still carries it; a `ctrl+r`
  key routed to the view does not clear it (criterion 3, second half).
- `TestEveryJobReporterIsRoutedToTheRegistry` keeps passing (no new Reporter).

Command: `go test ./internal/app -run 'Failure|Forget' && go test -race ./internal/app`

Done when: the above pass, the existing `internal/app` suite passes, `mise run lint`.

## Step 4 — Nothing is persisted (criterion 5)

Depends on: 2. Parallel with 3.

Files: `internal/jobs/nodisk_test.go` (new), `internal/app/failures_test.go` (one test).

Tests:
- `TestTheRegistryNeverTouchesTheDisk` (source test, `go/parser` over the non-test files
  of `internal/jobs`): fails, naming file and import, on `os`, `io/ioutil`,
  `github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/cache`, `…/internal/config`. `path/filepath` is
  allowed (pure). Same style as `TestNoViewStylesItsOwnFooterMessage`.
- `TestFailuresAreNotWrittenAnywhere` (`internal/app`, `isolateHome(t)`): build the
  router, `filepath.WalkDir(HOME)` → listing with sizes and mtimes; drive a failure,
  a retry, a second failure and a `ForgetTargetMsg` through `a.Update` (no Work executed:
  `StartMsg.Work` nil); walk again → identical. Then a fresh `routerAt` on the same HOME
  → `a.jobs.Failures()` empty (restart).

Command: `go test ./internal/jobs -run NeverTouches && go test ./internal/app -run NotWritten -count=2`

`-count=2` on purpose: HOME is process-shared in `internal/app` (DEVDESK-36), and
`isolateHome` is what keeps the second run honest.

Done when: both pass at `-count=2`.

## Step 5 — `app-shell.md`

Depends on: 2, 3 (describe what was built). Same PR, same commit as the code.

File: `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`, section "The jobs registry — `internal/jobs`":
- add `Failures()` and `Forget(target, context)` to the method table;
- new subsection `#### The last failure per target` covering: the key
  `(Kind, TargetKey(Target), Run.Context)`; written in `record` from `advance` and
  `Discover`, cleared at `Start`/`Discover`, at `done`, at `delete done` and by
  `ForgetTargetMsg` (current context, path descendants); one entry per key, 500 cap,
  oldest evicted, never on disk, independent of `MaxFinishedRuns`; `TargetKey` cleans
  absolute paths and keeps image references raw, with the three reasons above;
  `Item.Target` is not rewritten and why; `Kind.Remembered` and the answer to Q-A;
  D5 is the reader's (`FailuresOn(…, kinds...)`);
- in "The broadcast, and the one spinner chain": `ChangedMsg` also carries `Failures`,
  a copy;
- one sentence: `security.scanTarget.Failed` and OCI `failedScans` are the two manual
  copies this replaces, removed by A-08 and A-09a (not here).

Optional (techwriter): a short entry in `docs/backlog.md` §3 recording "image references
are not normalized in the failure key" as a decision, since it outlives this plan.

Done when: a reviewer can answer from the doc alone "why does a failure on `nginx` not
show on `docker.io/library/nginx`".

---

## Final check (whole PR)

```
mise run check            # fmt + vet + lint + test
mise run test-race        # internal/app and internal/jobs at least
go test ./internal/app -count=2
```

## Risks

| Risk | Level | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Some transitions put a raw `err.Error()` in `Detail` (clone `cloneEnded`/`cloneWalkFailed`, forge index); the memory stores it as is | medium, for A-05 | not A-04's to fix (it stores what `Item.Detail` already holds). A-05/A-10b must word the footer, Rule 128. Flag it to them. |
| A view emits a target spelled differently from the run's (not seen today) | low | `TargetKey` covers path spelling; reference spelling is by design one per engine/context |
| `ChangedMsg` copy at 10 Hz | low | bounded by 500; disappears with A-03 (`FrameMsg`) |
| A Forget arriving after a context switch clears the new context's key | low | the image remove is a short Cmd; stated as Hypothèse; carry `Context` on the message later if A-09a meets it |

No irreversible point: the memory is session-only; the key and helpers are internal APIs.

   - Un item `failed` pose l'échec, un item `done` l'efface.
   - Un `delete` réussi efface tous les types d'opération de la cible, ainsi que les chemins situés sous elle.
   - `Start` efface les clés admises. `Discover` efface aussi, car les cibles du clone sont admises là.
   - `skipped` et `Cancel` ne posent rien.
   - Au-delà de 500 clés, l'entrée la plus ancienne sort ; reposer une clé la rafraîchit.
   - API : `Failures()` (renvoie une copie), `Forget(target, ctx) bool` et `Kind.Remembered()`.
   - Le contexte vient du run retrouvé, ce qui tient aussi après un changement de contexte.
   - Test : `go test -race ./internal/jobs`.

   - même clé `ws` / `:sec` pour un dépôt, et `/w/app/` donne `/w/app` ;
   - même clé OCI / `:sec` pour `nginx:1.27` ;
   - aller-retour de contexte A → B → A ;
   - quitter puis rouvrir une vue, et `ctrl+r` : l'échec reste ;
   - `Forget` n'agit que dans le contexte courant.
   - Test : `go test ./internal/app -run 'Failure|Forget' && go test -race ./internal/app`.
4. **Rien sur disque** : un test lit le source et refuse les imports `os`, `io/ioutil`, `internal/cache` et `internal/config` dans `internal/jobs`. Un test du routeur avec `isolateHome` liste le contenu de HOME avant et après : il doit être identique. Un routeur recréé ensuite ne contient aucun échec. Les deux tournent avec `-count=2`.
5. **`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`**, dans le même commit que le code : nouvelle sous-section « The last failure per target », table des méthodes et paragraphe sur `ChangedMsg`.

**Identité de la cible (critère 8)** :
- **Les chemins absolus sont normalisés** par `filepath.Clean`. La normalisation ne s'applique qu'à la clé d'échec, à l'écriture comme à la lecture. `Item.Target` n'est pas réécrit : sinon `FindItem` ne retrouverait plus les transitions émises avec la cible brute, et la ligne tournerait sans fin.
- **Les références d'image ne sont pas normalisées** : `nginx` et `docker.io/library/nginx` donnent deux clés. Trois raisons :
  - la clé doit rester celle du cache de scan, une chaîne brute sur laquelle OCI et `:sec` s'accordent déjà ;
  - `Image.Name()` renvoie `nginx` sans tag quand le tag est `<none>`, et une normalisation le confondrait avec `nginx:latest` ;
  - l'orthographe dépend du moteur, qui est fixé par contexte : docker écrit `nginx`, podman `docker.io/library/nginx`. Comme un échec n'est montré que dans son contexte, il n'y a pas de conflit.
- Les images dont le dépôt est `<none>` ne sont jamais scannées ni tirées, elles n'arrivent donc pas dans le mémorisateur.

**Hypothèses prudentes** (signalées dans le plan) :
- `Forget` ne vise que le contexte courant, parce que le moteur de conteneurs se choisit par contexte.
- Les descendants ne sont effacés que pour les chemins de fichiers ; ni les chemins de forge ni les images.
- Une sync refusée (arbre modifié) est `skipped` : elle n'est pas mémorisée.

**Risque à transmettre à A-05 et A-10b** : les transitions du clone et de l'index de forge mettent `err.Error()` brut dans `Detail`. Le mémorisateur le garde tel quel, et c'est le texte du footer qui devra être formulé (Rule 128).

## Questions bloquantes

**Q-A (question ouverte 2) : quels types d'opération le mémorisateur garde-t-il ?** Les étapes 1 à 5 peuvent commencer sans la réponse : elle ne change que le corps de `Kind.Remembered()` et un tableau de test.
- **A, ma recommandation : tous les types.** Le filtrage D5 se fait à la lecture, il n'y a aucune liste à maintenir et un nouveau type est couvert sans rien faire. Le coût : les échecs `index` sont gardés alors qu'aucune vue ne les montre.
- B : seulement les types du tableau D5 (scan, sync, delete, pull, create, clone), sans `index`.
- C : le scan seul. Dans ce cas A-07, A-09a, A-10 et A-11 devraient chacune rouvrir A-04.

Ce qui décide : la table indicative du critère 9 est-elle la liste définitive de ce que chaque vue affiche ? Si oui, c'est A ou B, qui ne diffèrent que par `index`. Si seuls les échecs de scan doivent durer, c'est C.

5. **`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`**, dans le même commit que le code : nouvelle sous-section « The last failure per target », table des méthodes et paragraphe sur `ChangedMsg`.

**Identité de la cible (critère 8)** :
- **Les chemins absolus sont normalisés** par `filepath.Clean`. La normalisation ne s'applique qu'à la clé d'échec, à l'écriture comme à la lecture. `Item.Target` n'est pas réécrit : sinon `FindItem` ne retrouverait plus les transitions émises avec la cible brute, et la ligne tournerait sans fin.
- **Les références d'image ne sont pas normalisées** : `nginx` et `docker.io/library/nginx` donnent deux clés. Trois raisons :
  - la clé doit rester celle du cache de scan, une chaîne brute sur laquelle OCI et `:sec` s'accordent déjà ;
  - `Image.Name()` renvoie `nginx` sans tag quand le tag est `<none>`, et une normalisation le confondrait avec `nginx:latest` ;
  - l'orthographe dépend du moteur, qui est fixé par contexte : docker écrit `nginx`, podman `docker.io/library/nginx`. Comme un échec n'est montré que dans son contexte, il n'y a pas de conflit.
- Les images dont le dépôt est `<none>` ne sont jamais scannées ni tirées, elles n'arrivent donc pas dans le mémorisateur.

**Hypothèses prudentes** (signalées dans le plan) :
- `Forget` ne vise que le contexte courant, parce que le moteur de conteneurs se choisit par contexte.
- Les descendants ne sont effacés que pour les chemins de fichiers ; ni les chemins de forge ni les images.
- Une sync refusée (arbre modifié) est `skipped` : elle n'est pas mémorisée.

**Risque à transmettre à A-05 et A-10b** : les transitions du clone et de l'index de forge mettent `err.Error()` brut dans `Detail`. Le mémorisateur le garde tel quel, et c'est le texte du footer qui devra être formulé (Rule 128).

## Questions bloquantes

**Q-A (question ouverte 2) : quels types d'opération le mémorisateur garde-t-il ?** Les étapes 1 à 5 peuvent commencer sans la réponse : elle ne change que le corps de `Kind.Remembered()` et un tableau de test.
- **A, ma recommandation : tous les types.** Le filtrage D5 se fait à la lecture, il n'y a aucune liste à maintenir et un nouveau type est couvert sans rien faire. Le coût : les échecs `index` sont gardés alors qu'aucune vue ne les montre.
- B : seulement les types du tableau D5 (scan, sync, delete, pull, create, clone), sans `index`.
- C : le scan seul. Dans ce cas A-07, A-09a, A-10 et A-11 devraient chacune rouvrir A-04.

Ce qui décide : la table indicative du critère 9 est-elle la liste définitive de ce que chaque vue affiche ? Si oui, c'est A ou B, qui ne diffèrent que par `index`. Si seuls les échecs de scan doivent durer, c'est C.
